summary.headline: Nitin Spinners Q2 FY27 revenue rose 29.6% YoY to INR985.2 crore and EBITDA margin hit 17.8%, with capex commissioning slated for December 2026.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue (third consecutive record), driven by higher yarn realisation, stable demand and higher fabric volumes. EBITDA rose 76.3% YoY to INR175.5 crore, with margin at 17.8%, flat QoQ and up 471 bps YoY. Management said trial production of about 41 lakh meters of fabric contributed roughly INR21 crore of revenue at a small EBITDA loss, so ex-trial margin was about 18.5%. Expansion commissioning is on schedule for end-December 2026, with renewable capacity rising from 41 MW to about 95 MW.

financial_highlights.change: +471 bps YoY vs 13.1%; flat vs Q1 FY27 (17.78%)
+57% YoY vs INR210.8 crore; margin +423 bps
+116.4% YoY vs INR75.8 crore; EPS INR29.16, cash EPS INR42.65

segments.name: Spinning (yarn)
segments.commentary: Utilisation over 98% in Q2 FY27; yarn realisation up about 12.5-13% QoQ per management's errata. Management also said about 80% of spinning capacity is currently utilised, with 17-18% of capacity closed, which conflicts with the 98% figure and needs clarification.

segments.name: Woven fabric
segments.commentary: Record quarterly fabric revenue; utilisation about 90%. Fabric realisation up about 6% QoQ per errata, lagging yarn price increases. Post-expansion, 28-30% of yarn capacity is dedicated to woven fabric.

segments.name: Knitting (greige)
segments.commentary: Utilisation fell due to the stop in new US orders after proposed 100% US duty and weak fabric pricing versus yarn; knitting is under 2% of total investment and largely depreciated. Management says profitability impact is not major.

segments.name: Trial production (new fabric capacity)
segments.commentary: About 41 lakh meters produced, INR21 crore revenue and about INR1 crore EBITDA loss in Q2; management expects about INR300-350 crore of added revenue in FY27 and about INR1,000 crore annually from FY28.

guidance_outlook: Commercial production in all divisions expected by end-December 2026; spinning utilisation to reach 95%+ by end-March 2027; finished fabric capacity to take 8-9 months more to reach full levels (around August-September 2027).

Management expects EBITDA margin to stay around the 18-18.5% level; longer-run band cited as 16-20%, with management saying it is in the middle of the range and the first objective is to sustain current margins.
Depreciation to rise from about INR37.5-38 crore per quarter to INR53-54 crore per quarter after expansion, and to about INR200 crore plus in FY28.
Revenue aspiration of INR4,800-5,000 crore by FY29 from existing assets plus modernisation; FY28 capex of INR80-100 crore for modernisation and balancing.
Renewable energy capacity to rise from 41 MW to about 95 MW by end-December 2026, meeting 50-55% of power needs; a further push toward about 65% is planned for FY28.
capex_capacity: Partial trials have started in all expansion segments; commercial production in all divisions is expected by end-December 2026.
Post-expansion, spinning capacity is planned at 28-30% dedicated to woven fabric (in-house yarn consumption to rise).

Peak term debt expected at about INR1,440 crore in March 2027, with working capital about INR400 crore rising to INR500 crore plus; total debt about INR1,950 crore. Annual repayments INR180-200 crore for 6-7 years.
Interest subsidy of about 2.5% on average is expected on new capex loans; blended cost of debt 6.5-6.75%.
Management has not yet decided on the next expansion (garmenting is only an aspiration); the next step is modernisation and balancing, expected to add about 5% capacity.
demand_pricing: Domestic cotton rose to about INR67,000-68,000 per candy on lower arrivals and deficient rainfall; international cotton at about USD0.80/lb and expected to average USD0.84-0.85 (range USD0.75-0.90). Import duty exemption extended for about half the year.
Average yarn count realisation about INR125-130/kg in Q2, broadly unchanged currently; domestic cotton kept at par with international prices, keeping spreads healthy.
Export revenue grew over 40% YoY, attributed to USD depreciation, about 20-25% higher yarn realisation, and some diversion from domestic to export markets; Bangladesh demand described as stable.
Cost pressures noted on dyes, chemicals, coal, packaging, freight and sea freight, which management expects to partly offset through pricing and scale; fabric price pass-through is slow.
Monthly revenue run-rate is about INR300 crore; Q2 carry-over from late dispatch was INR35-40 crore, described as routine variation.

qa_highlights.question: Spread in Q2 and outlook given new domestic cotton supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Average yarn count realisation was about INR125-130/kg in Q2, and levels are broadly unchanged currently.

qa_highlights.question: Why was EBITDA margin flat QoQ and what was the one-off from new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production added INR21 crore revenue and a roughly INR1 crore EBITDA loss; excluding this, margin would be about 18.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the debt levels and repayment profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Term debt to peak at about INR1,440 crore in March 2027, working capital INR400-500 crore, total about INR1,950 crore, with repayments of INR180-200 crore a year for 6-7 years.

qa_highlights.question: How much incremental revenue will the new fabric capacity add?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR300-350 crore in FY27 and about INR1,000 crore a year from FY28, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise about 40% since March?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly export receivables from higher exports; no extra credit given, and fewer bill discounting limits were utilised. No major overdues, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why is knitting utilisation low?
qa_highlights.answer: Stopped US orders after a proposed 100% US duty, plus fabric prices lagging yarn; knitting is under 2% of investment and mostly depreciated.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (dyes, chemicals, coal, packaging, freight) and slow pass-through to fabric prices could compress the 18-18.5% margin.
Ramp-up of new fabric and spinning capacity from December 2026; finished fabric may take until about August-September 2027 to reach full utilisation.
Cotton import duty exemption is only extended for about half the year; policy continuity is uncertain.
Rising receivables (about 40% since March, mainly exports) and higher working capital and debt (total about INR1,950 crore by March 2027).
Bangladesh wage-agitation shutdowns and US tariff uncertainty affecting knitting and export orders.
Management declined to share order book details; spinning utilisation (98% stated vs about 80% also stated) needs clarification.
summary.management_tone: Confident on current results and the expansion timeline, but cautious on margin extrapolation, citing input cost pressures and slow fabric pass-through. Evasive on order book and on the next capex decision, which is still undecided.
key_quotes: Q2 FY27 has been another strong all -around quarter for the company.
We have not guided for 20%. First of all, Varun ji, I would like to highlight that.
As far as the upper level or upper -- it is always the endeavor of the company to reach the top level of margins. But still, I think we are far from there.

adds.what: Expansion across spinning and woven fabric (new fabric capacity in trial production; commercial production in all divisions by end-Dec 2026)
Renewable energy capacity from 41 MW to about 95 MW
Modernisation and balancing (next expansion step, not yet decided)

growth.why: Management guides INR300-350 crore incremental revenue in FY27 and about INR1,000 crore annually from FY28 from expansion commissioning by end-December 2026, with spinning utilisation to reach 95%+ by end-March 2027; backing is specific on timing and capacity but not on firm orders, and the brief has internal inconsistencies (98% vs ~80% spinning utilisation) that need clarification.
